## Introduction

For this portfolio we'll be recreating one of the classic "ridge-line" plots or "joy plots" that show changes in mothers age of birth through time.

This is usually done with US data to highlight the baby boom, but we'll be using the Aotearoa/NZ data instead, by cohort:

```{r}
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)

nz_births <- read_csv("https://www.massey.ac.nz/~jcmarsha/data/nz/births_tidy.csv") |>
  mutate(cohort = year - age) |> # mothers year of birth
  filter(cohort >= 1948, cohort <= 1980, age < 46)
```


## Requirements

Download the `portfolio03.qmd` template file below and **modify** the existing figure code to produce a unique, eye-catching chart with the same geometry type.

 - Ensure you fill in your name in the author field.
 - Keep the same geometry (`geom_slab()`) but instead focus on the presentation.
 - Your chart must have appropriate labels and a title.
 - You must use a theme for your chart that is unique: any pre-existing theme used must be modified.
 - You must utilise a non-standard font which is acquired via `require_font()` from an online source (for reproducibility).
 - You must utilise a colour in your chart in some way. This needn't be mapped to an aesthetic (though can be if you wish).
 - You must alter the aspect ratio or dimensions of the figure.
 - You should submit the `portfolio03.qmd` file to the stream dropbox.
 - Make sure that it renders correctly before submission.
 
## Grading rubric

You will be graded out of 10 based on:

 - Your submission must be reproducible and render without errors or warnings (2 marks).
 - Your submission must include your name in the author field and the code for your chart (2 marks).
 - Your chart should satisfy the requirements given above (6 marks).
